purpose: Define the citizen-facing lifecycle after evidence is submitted, from receipt through identity/property/date validation, sufficiency assessment, conflict handling and next action.
core_principle: RECEIVED → IDENTIFIED → MATCHED → VALIDATED → ASSESSED → WHAT_IT_ESTABLISHES → WHAT_REMAINS → NEXT
rules: Citizen-supplied evidence remains labelled as such until independently validated.
Property matching and date matching are separate checks.
An item can be sufficient for one proposition but insufficient for another.
A conflict is preserved rather than silently resolved.
Access restriction is not evidence absence.
Validation does not rewrite historical records.
Only validated facts enter the approved answer/evidence layer.
Privacy is checked before any public exposure.
The citizen is told what happens next based on the actual recorded state.
hard_stops: Never mark evidence validated merely because it was uploaded.
Never treat a user document as an official record without validation.
Never infer property identity from filename or address alone.
Never infer date match from an undated document.
Never promise that submitted evidence will change the answer.
Never expose restricted or unnecessary personal data.
